gap: No result ChatGPT got states the parking-ready total for any 4K front-and-rear kit (camera plus the maker's own hardwire kit, plus a card where none is in the box), so none shows which kits still land under $250 once parking mode is wired.
standout_why: Compared against Product Bible (front-and-rear), RoadGearLab, The Gadgeteer, Digital Camera World and knowledgelib; Car and Driver could not be fetched. Product Bible says all seven of its cameras need a hardwire kit and names HK4/HK6 but prints no kit price and no total. RoadGearLab gives bitrates and hours on a 256 GB card (A229 Pro about 6.9 h, A810S about 14.4 h) but no kit price or total. The Gadgeteer gives the ROVE Dual Pro at $206.49 with a free 128 GB card and no kit price. knowledgelib and Digital Camera World state no kit price or all-in cost. ChatGPT's own answer only warns that extras 'can push a $220 camera above $250' without a figure. Limit on this finding: Shopify returned HTTP 429 on every product page I tried, so the rival camera prices below come from each store's own search listing and the variant is not confirmed; the single-item hardwire kit prices are firmer.
decides: With parking mode wired, the linked DDPAI N5 Pro (2-channel: 4K front + 1440p rear) comes to $187.51 and needs no card because of its 64 GB eMMC, so it wins the 'parking-ready under $250 with storage included' segment. The VIOFO A229 Pro 2CH was listed at $349.99 on viofo.com today; at Product Bible's Amazon price of $219.99 (their read, 2026-11-19) it is $237.98 with the HK4 and has no card in the box, leaving $12.02 for one. The DDPAI Z90 Pro ($266.71) and Vantrue S1 Pro Max 4K+4K ($264.98) are under $250 as cameras but cross it once the maker's kit is added. This confirms the A229 Pro as the image-quality pick only at the Amazon sale price and without much room for a card.
